5.text: sometimes quite abnormal. The Russianized Yukaghir and Yakut of the

6.text: Lower Kolyma, until very recently, had to pay eleven rubles for each male.

7.text: No such thing is possible among the Chukchee. The greater the distance

8.text: from Russian villages, the smaller the number of families who are willing to

9.text: pay tribute. The largest portion of the tribute allotted to each clan is paid

10.text: by the so-called “chief.” It is not so very difficult for a rich Chukchee to

27.text: FAMILY. — The Chukchee family usually consists of a husband, with one

28.text: or several wives and their children. Generally the parents of the man live

29.text: near by in a lodging of their own; and with them may live younger sons

30.text: and daughters, who are not yet married, or, if married, have no children.

33.text: POSITION OF OLD PEOPLE. — Old men usually enjoy great consideration.

34.text: Especially is this the case among the reindeer-breeding part of the tribe,

35.text: perhaps because the herd is the property of the father as long as he lives.

36.text: It seems that among all nomadic tribes there is a tendency to develop strong

37.text: family and family-group ties, and that with this phenomenon is connected the

38.text: high position of the old men of the family. Although I cannot make the

39.text: general assertion that the organization of family and family-group is more

40.text: highly developed among the Reindeer Chukchee than among the Maritime
